Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Transient stimulus, delayed re-challenge (hysteresis test)
ideas.description: Expose cells (e.g., fibroblasts or macrophages) to a defined pulse of AP-1-activating signal (TPA, TNF, or injury), wash out, then re-stimulate after days to weeks and measure transcriptional response by RNA-seq and nascent-transcript assays. Memory predicts faster or stronger induction of specific genes than in naive cells, and the effect should be lost if c-Jun/c-Fos is knocked out (e.g., degron) only during the first pulse.

ideas.title: Case-switching chromatin accessibility: 'upper vs lower case' states
ideas.description: Use ATAC-seq/CUT&Tag for AP-1 factors (FOS, JUN), H3K27ac and H3K4me1 before, immediately after, and long after stimulus to find enhancers that stay open or primed once AP-1 has left, like type that stays set after the hand moves on. Test causality by showing those enhancers are AP-1 motif-dependent via CRISPR motif mutation or dCas9 perturbation and that persistent accessibility predicts the enhanced re-response.

ideas.title: Single-cell tracking of AP-1 dynamics with live reporters
ideas.description: Tag endogenous FOS/JUN (or use a synthetic AP-1 reporter) and image single cells over days to determine whether memory is stored as sustained AP-1 activity, a self-sustaining feedback loop, or as heritable chromatin marks after AP-1 returns to baseline. Correlating prior pulse history with later per-cell response and lineage inheritance across divisions separates cell-autonomous memory from population effects.

ideas.title: Acute degron-based necessity and sufficiency with timing control
ideas.description: Use inducible degradation of AP-1 (e.g., dTAG on JUN/FOS or dominant-negative A-FOS) at different windows: during priming, during the memory interval, and during re-challenge. If AP-1 is needed only to establish memory, removal during the interval will have no effect, whereas needing it to maintain memory implies ongoing presence; also test sufficiency by transient ectopic expression of AP-1 in naive cells.

ideas.title: Tightness metric: dose-dependence and decay kinetics of memory
ideas.description: Quantify how memory scales with pulse strength, duration and number of repeats, and measure its half-life and persistence across cell divisions, forming a quantitative model (e.g., bistable vs graded) of how much 'spacing' is needed to lock the state. Fit the data with a dynamical model and verify its predictions, such as bistability with a threshold, by sorting cells and checking for bimodal, heritable states.
